claim_summary: Cinnamon powder was tested in spirulina-enriched cookies, flakes and dried noodles. Selected additions were 10%, 2.5% and 2.5% respectively. Methods report 9.5% dried spirulina and 0/2.5/5/7.5/10% cinnamon by weight. Complete recipe masses and finished yield are not established here; this does not validate 1% cinnamon in our bar.
notes: Full methods checked 2026-10-24. Correct study-material join; no dose bound created.

claim_summary: Seventeen spirulina samples (16 commercial products and one raw biomass) contained 128 identified VOCs by HS-SPME-GC-MS. The largest classes were alkanes, ketones, aldehydes and alcohols. The figures are relative areas, not concentrations, and they vary by product.
notes: Source checked 2026-10-24. Not approved. Table 3 odor descriptors are cited from references 37/38; not measured sensory responses in these samples. Relative areas are not concentrations or proof of odor activity.

claim_summary: The snack-bar paper labels treatments 0/2/3/4/5% spirulina. Table 5 reports 20 panelists and a seven-point liking scale. Overall acceptance shares the same significance letter across treatments; aroma letters differ despite the narrative reporting no significant aroma effect. This inconsistency needs review; no named off-note reduction was measured.
notes: Avoid blanket no-sensory-effect claim. Not evidence for this project's recipe.
